top_issues: WETH detail: 0.00 balance dominates over the accounts card, so the only real money (+115.00 owes you) is secondary; the H1 hub chip and 'send up to 175.00 / receive up to 0.50' pair is small and easy to misread as a balance.
The 'RECENT' list mixes five different states (closed/open/settled/settled) with only a tiny dot + word, so at a glance it reads as noise.
fixes: When an account like H1 has a nonzero 'owes you', promote it above the zero WETH card and auto-open it; make 'owes you +115.00' the headline figure.
Give each recent row a small colored left bar matching the account legend (green=violet/gray) so state is readable without reading text.

top_issues: 'Spendable now $175.00' is larger than the 'Total balance $155.00' above it — a user will read this as the product being wrong or letting them spend money they do not have.
The 'Two colours, one rule' explainer occupies prime screen real estate above the action buttons and is not dismissible in the visible state.
fixes: Rename 'Spendable now' to 'Available to send (incl. credit room)' with a one-line caption: 'includes $175 you can use on hub credit' so it never exceeds total without explanation.
Make the explainer a one-time primer (dismiss to a small '?' legend) so the Pay/Receive/Swap row and balances sit above the fold.

top_issues: The '2 ROUTES' section is good, but the two cards only differ by a tiny fee (0.000050 vs 0.000075) and a route hop (H1→H2 vs H1→H3→H2); the 'You send 25.00' line is identical, so the tradeoff (fee vs hops) is not explained.
The amount bar 'send up to 180.00 / receive up to 23.00' is fine but the relationship between 'This payment 25.00' and 'Your account with H1 120.00' is unclear.
fixes: Add a one-line hint under the route selection: 'lower fee via H1; H3 adds a hop for a slightly higher fee but more optionality'.
Label the bar's right edge 'receive up to' as the hub credit room, not a money figure, to avoid it being read as spendable balance.

top_issues: Fee is shown as 'under 0.01 USDC' here but as an exact amount (0.000050) on the expanded routes view — inconsistent precision on the same action.
'Up to 175.00 instantly' and the bar right edge 'receive up to 0.50' are small, and the amount entry lacks a max/clear affordance beyond the bar.
fixes: Show the exact fee (0.000050 USDC) consistently on both the collapsed and expanded route views.
Add a 'Max' button next to the amount and enlarge the 'Up to 175.00' label for single-handed reading.

top_issues: The receipt sheet is strong, but the four action buttons (Copy receipt / Download / Print·PDF / Done) are cramped in a row; on a 360px-wide phone 'Copy receipt' and 'Print / PDF' will wrap or clip.
The background now shows $130.00 (post-payment) but the receipt is for 25.00 — a user scanning only the sheet may not connect the two.
fixes: Make the action row a 2x2 grid (Copy / Download / Print / Done) with fixed 50% width and consistent icon+label so none wrap.
Add a small 'balance now $130.00' line under the Paid heading to anchor the receipt in the new total.

top_issues: The trust block is excellent (PAID, 25.00, to H2 via H1, Frame #81, Proof, Verified by your runtime), but 'in 9s' and 'Verified by your runtime' are small and could be missed by a novice.
The proof hash '0x00109fe5...6bec' is truncated with no copy affordance on this sheet — a compliance user needs the full value.
fixes: Increase the 'in 9s / Verified by your runtime' line size and set it in green to match the trusted-state color.
Make the truncated proof hash tappable to reveal and copy the full value, and add it to the Copy receipt payload.

top_issues: 'YOUR ENTITY ID' shows a long truncated hex (0xbad0865d...67985a) and the paragraph 'Anyone with an account route to you' is jargon-heavy for a receive flow.
The 'What is this for?' placeholder for Note is vague and reads as unfinished rather than a hint.
fixes: Replace the entity-id paragraph with 'Payments arrive instantly up to your inbound room' and put the full entity id behind a copy button.
Change the Note placeholder to 'e.g. lunch, rent' so it reads as an example, not an empty affordance.

top_issues: The QR is well-proportioned and high-contrast (good), but '25.50 capacity via H1' is small and the 'Amount·optional 0.00' placeholder is low-contrast gray.
'Prepare incoming account H1·Testnet' is a card that looks tappable but has no explanatory value for a novice (what does preparing do?).
fixes: Enlarge 'capacity via H1' and darken the 0.00 placeholder so it still reads as editable.
Add one line under 'Prepare incoming account': 'sets up the hub account that will hold what you receive'.

top_issues: The book ladder is excellent (price/size, live·relay, spread, tick rule), but the selected mid row (2498.5000, 13.6000) is highlighted only by a faint background — the selection is not obvious as 'your chosen fill'.
The '1 tick = 1/10,000 USDC' footnote is useful but small; without it the price precision (2500.5000) is unreadable to a non-expert.
fixes: Give the focused book row a left accent bar and a 'fill' affordance (e.g. an arrow) so tapping is clearly an action.
Move the '1 tick' rule into the header as a second line under 'PRICE USDC' so it is always visible.

top_issues: The fee/tariff paragraph ('Gross receive: 0.039992 WETH before fees. H1 collateral tariff: 0.1 WETH base + 0 WETH gas + 1 bps...') is a dense wall of copy that buries the actual net number.
'You receive 0.039992' is large, but the 6-decimal precision plus 'Quoted at the best price in the book right now' is a lot to parse at once.
fixes: Replace the tariff paragraph with a 3-row table (Fee / Collateral / Net) and surface 'Net receive 0.0399…' as the prominent figure.
Round the big receive number to 4 significant digits for the headline and keep full precision only in the detail line.

top_issues: The credit-limit-extension flow (collateral slider, 'Add 10% buffer', 'Available 0.00 WETH·Need 0.00798 WETH more') is heavy cognitive load — the slider and the hard number conflict and the buffer checkbox adds a math step.
The red 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' warning is correct but creates a dead-end: the user must approve credit before the swap can proceed, and the two-step connection is not obvious.
fixes: Replace the slider+buffer with three preset cards (100% / 50% / 0% collateral) and drop the buffer checkbox into a default-on note, so it is one decision not three.
Add a 'Continue swap →' affordance that enables after the credit step so the user sees this as a gate, not an error.

top_issues: The cross-network model (Testnet → H1 → Tron, 'Atomic·both legs or neither') is well presented but dense; '0.007998' is a tiny receive number and 'into your Tron account' requires the user to already understand the two-account structure.
'Your other account Main Tron·Tron / Hub there H3' is correct but reads as a third hop in the route rather than a destination account.
fixes: Give the route pill a single destination label '→ Tron (via H1)' and move 'Your other account' into a separate 'Destination' card so the route and the account are not conflated.
Add a 'Net receive' figure on the same line as the big number so the atomic guarantee has a concrete amount.

top_issues: 'They owe you, uncovered $90.00 / Cover it' is excellent risk data, but the purple 'Cover it' is ambiguous — does it move the $90 into collateral or extend credit?
The bottom nav overlaps the last card (the 'Every frame here is signed...' footer is partially hidden behind the Home tab).
fixes: Rename 'Cover it' to 'Post collateral to cover' so the action is explicit, and add a one-line preview of the result.
Add safe-area bottom padding so content never sits under the tab bar on dense screens.

top_issues: This is the strongest risk screen: credit lines to them / collateral posted / owes you all clear. But the six action buttons render 3+2 (Pay/Extend credit/Swap, then Manage/Dispute) which is an inconsistent grid.
The legend now has five states (secured/promised/you owe/credit room/in flight) while the home explainer teaches only 'two colours, one rule' — a direct contradiction.
fixes: Make it a 2x3 grid so all six buttons align identically (Pay / Extend credit / Swap / Manage / Dispute / + another).
Extend the home legend to include 'you owe (amber) / credit room (gray) / in flight (hatched)' or reduce account coloring to the two-rule set on this screen.

top_issues: The dispute sheet is correct but the full-screen overlay dims the underlying account heavily, which can feel ominous; the 3-step explanation is dense and reads as legal copy.
'Dispute this account...' in red is good, but there is no confirmation of what is reversible versus irreversible before the tap.
fixes: Add a one-line 'This freezes the account and posts the last co-signed state on-chain; it cannot be undone' right above the button so the consequence precedes the action.
Keep the 3-step copy but shorten each step to one line with the key number (e.g. 'H1 has 1d to answer').

top_issues: The tabs (Collateral / Credit / Add token / Dispute) are clear and 'Dispute' is correctly the focused one here, but the explanatory paragraph uses 'freezes, withdraws your orders, puts the latest signed state on-chain' — a lot of new concepts at once.
The numbered 1-2-3 steps are readable, but the 'H1 has 1d to answer' wording implies an arbitrary countdown.
fixes: Shorten the intro to 'Freezes the account and posts the last state you both signed on-chain.' and move the orders-withdrawal note to a secondary line.
Replace '1d' with 'you have 1 day for H1 to respond' in a dedicated callout so the window is explicit.

top_issues: The header 'Today·in $140.00·out $68.58·5 movements / 7 movements' is cramped and confusing — the '5 movements' vs '7 movements' depends on an in/out calculation the user has to infer.
The filter chips overflow (Accou… truncated) and 'All' is the only obvious default; the scrollable chip row is not discoverable.
fixes: Simplify the header to 'Today: in $140.00 · out $68.58 · 7 movements' on one line so the count is unambiguous.
Collapse the filter chips to a horizontal scroll with a visible fade or overflow chevron so 'Accounts' is not cut off.

top_issues: The receipt detail is excellent (-25.00 USDC, Frame #81, Proof, '2 committed entries', runtime verification). The 'To 0x92c2d7...cbf0' is truncated with no copy affordance.
'Frames 2 committed entries' is a strong proof line but the wording is insider-language; a non-technical user won't know what 'committed entries' means.
fixes: Make the truncated 'To' hash tappable to copy the full value, mirroring the receipt sheet.
Change '2 committed entries' to '2 signed records' and keep 'committed' only in the detail so the trust meaning is clear.

top_issues: The 'AT THIS SCALE' illustration uses blue bars to show $100→$100,000, but the product's balance language is green/violet — this is a color-language inconsistency on the very screen that teaches the scale.
'Reveal recovery phrase' is the most sensitive button in the app and it sits directly beside 'Lock'; the two are too close and the phrase reveal has no warning banner.
fixes: Recolor the scale example bars using the green (yours) / violet (promise) palette so the scale lesson matches the balances.
Separate 'Reveal recovery phrase' from 'Lock' with a divider and add a 'Only do this on a private device' warning above it.

top_issues: The scale controls are numerous (slider + Auto + six preset buttons + live '1 px = $10' label) — more controls than the single decision they serve.
The three HOME toggles (On-chain wallet / Reserve / Accounts) are described with prose that reads more like a protocol diagram than a user setting.
fixes: Reduce the scale UI to the slider plus the current preset highlighted on it, dropping the six separate preset buttons to a single 'presets' row.
Shorten toggle descriptions to 4-5 words each (e.g. 'On-chain wallet — slow, fully yours') and keep the long text on the Manage/Sovereignty explainers.

top_issues: 'WHAT HAPPENS / Fund you through H1' is a good educational block, but the explanation ('Reserve to account posts collateral on-chain; the account can then be used instantly') is a long single sentence with no visual anchor.
The block leaves large empty space, making the screen feel unfinished.
fixes: Split the explanation into two short labeled lines: '1. Posts collateral on-chain' / '2. Account becomes usable instantly' so it scans quickly.
Remove the excess vertical padding so the Sign & send button stays above the fold.

top_issues: The FROM/TO card grids are clear, but when the user selects Reserve (40.00) as FROM and Account (150.00) as TO, the two bars use different value scales, so the 40 vs 150 is not visually comparable.
'Recipient entity·leave empty for yourself' is a confusing placeholder — a novice does not know what an entity id is or why it is optional.
fixes: Render FROM and TO bars on the same scale so a 40→150 move is visually obvious as a transfer, not two unrelated amounts.
Replace the placeholder with 'To: your own account (leave blank)' and a helper 'or paste a hub / friend id'.

top_issues: 'WHERE YOUR MONEY STANDS' is the clearest risk summary in the product (Total / Yours whatever a hub does / Promised by hubs / You owe) — excellent. The four tiles use a 'M' Manage bottom-nav icon that overlaps the Accounts card on scroll.
The 'Promised by hubs $90.00' in violet is visually prominent; a novice may read violet as money when it is a promise, though the caption helps.
fixes: Add bottom safe-area padding so the tile grid and Accounts card never sit under the tab bar.
Bold 'promise' in the violet caption ('Violet is a hub's promise — move it into collateral or dispute if the hub misbehaves') so the risk framing lands.

top_issues: The visible 'FAUCETS / Test money from the network you are connected to' frames funds as test money, which undercuts the trust the rest of the app builds — on a mainnet user this is alarming.
The faucet cards inherit the same premium styling as real asset rows, so a user may not realize these are non-value test funds.
fixes: Visually de-emphasize the faucet section (dashed border or a 'testnet' badge) so it cannot be mistaken for real balance.
Add a 'This network is Testnet' banner at the top of Assets so the faucet framing is unambiguous.

top_issues: The only nonzero figure on a page titled Assets is 'Gas 0.1000 ETH', which is a surprising focal point; the three token balances (USDC/WETH/USDT) are all 0.00 and the 'Depository may pull 0.00' line is small.
USDC (blue) and USDT (green) share the same '$' glyph, so at a glance the two tokens are not differentiable without reading the ticker.
fixes: Keep gas as a secondary line and add a 'Total asset value' headline so the page communicates a balance, not just a gas figure.
Differentiate token icons (USDC = $ circle, USDT = ₮ or a distinct color already present) so the pair is distinguishable without reading.

top_issues: 'H1 POOL / Available / Borrowed / Active principal' shows zeros and 'Refresh', but there is no indication of what the pool pays the lender or the pool's utilization — the economics are opaque until you scroll back to the terms.
The bottom nav overlaps the 'interest come back...' footer text.
fixes: Add a 'Pool rate' or 'APY' line to the H1 POOL card so lending value is visible on the same screen as the pool state.
Add bottom safe-area padding so the footer is never clipped by the tab bar.

top_issues: 'Amount to lend 0.00' is the default and 'Offer to the pool' is disabled (muted) — correct, but the '= 1.00% per term' conversion sits far to the right of '100' basis points, so the two readings of the interest are not visually linked.
The 1 hour / 1 day / 1 month term chips are clear, but there is no default 'term' shown as selected for a first-time lender.
fixes: Put '= 1.00% per term' directly under the '100' value, not on the far-right, so the basis-points-to-percent link is immediate.
Preselect '1 day' as the default term so the form is not empty and the Offer button can be evaluated.

top_issues: The ownership model (Entity / Kind / Threshold 1 of 1 / Signer) is clearly explained, but the prose ('a board can grow to several signers with a quorum... a lost key never means a lost entity') is long and reads like a capabilities doc.
The 'TAKE CONTROL OF ANOTHER ENTITY' card is empty and says 'nothing to take over' — useful but takes a screen slot for an empty state.
fixes: Cut the board paragraph to one sentence and move the quorum detail to a tooltip, so the screen reads as a fact sheet not a spec.
Keep the empty card but collapse it to a single line 'No other entity lists your signer' so the empty state does not dominate.

top_issues: 'Can dispute without asking 1 of 1' and 'Accounts co-signed 1 of 1' are the most meaningful trust lines, but they are small and the '1 of 1' reads as a fraction to a novice.
The bottom nav clips the per-counterparty line ('they answer in 1d·you in 1d'), losing the counterparty-most-relevant trust info.
fixes: Enlarge the '1 of 1' indicators and add a one-line gloss 'you can open a dispute on your own' under them.
Add safe-area padding so the per-counterparty row is never hidden by the tab bar.

top_issues: 'Enforceable right now $40.00' is the single clearest risk figure in the product, and the green/violet legend plus 'Green is yours whatever anyone does; violet is what a counterparty owes you on their signature alone' is genuinely excellent.
The long green/violet engineering explanation is dense for a first visit, but it is the right place for it; the only real issue is that 'Enforceable right now' is a phrase a novice must interpret.
fixes: Add a one-line caption under 'Enforceable right now': 'what you could withdraw today even if a hub vanished' so the term is self-explanatory.
Keep the legend but collapse the multi-sentence explanation behind a 'How this works' disclosure to reduce first-view density.

overall.verdict: A genuinely premium dark fintech UI with an outstanding color-coded state model (green = yours, violet = hub promise) and the best trust/evidence surfaces I have reviewed — receipts carry frame + proof + runtime verification, and Sovereignty breaks enforceability down per counterparty. The main drag is dense protocol jargon and two contradictions ('Spendable now' exceeding 'Total balance'; 'two colours, one rule' versus the five-state account legend) that hurt novices far more than they hurt the expert personas this product is built for.
priority_fixes: Reconcile 'Spendable now $175.00' with 'Total balance $155.00' on Home — add a one-line caption ('includes credit room') or rename it 'Available to send (incl. credit room)' so it never reads as money the user doesn't have (helps Rosa, Lucas, Priya).

Unify the color legend: either extend the Home 'two colours, one rule' primer to include you-owe/credit-room/in-flight, or reduce the account screen to the two-rule set — the current contradiction is the single most damaging consistency issue (helps Noah, Ingrid, Omar).
Replace the dense swap tariff paragraph with a 3-row table (Fee / Collateral / Net) and surface 'Net receive' as the prominent figure instead of burying it in prose (helps Wei, Aisha, Lucas).

Fix bottom-nav overlap on dense screens (account, activity, lend, sovereignty) with safe-area padding so the last content card — often the most trust-relevant ('they answer in 1d') — is never hidden (helps Elena, Ingrid).

Standardize action-button grids (account 3+2, receipt 4-in-a-row) to a consistent 2x2 or 2x3 layout so buttons align and labels never wrap on narrow phones (helps everyone, especially one-handed Rosa).

personas.name: Rosa
personas.verdict: The big $155 and the big Pay button are clear, but the app keeps telling me I can spend $175 when my total is $155, and every swap and cross-network screen is a wall of words I can't follow.
blockers: Home: 'Spendable now $175.00' exceeds 'Total balance $155.00' — reads as a bug
'Two colours, one rule' legend uses 'reserve / on-chain / secured / promised' jargon
Pay: 'send up to 175.00 / receive up to 0.50' small text and credit-room bar
Swap (both variants): tariff paragraph and route model are unreadable at a glance
No screen that says 'your money is safe' in one plain sentence — the closest is Sovereignty's 'Enforceable right now $40.00'

personas.name: Jamal
personas.verdict: I can see every payment land with a 'settled' dot and a proof, and the Move screen lets me push the week's cash somewhere safe — good enough that I'd keep using it, though the activity header is confusing.
blockers: Activity: header 'in $140.00·out $68.58·5 movements / 7 movements' — the two counts don't obviously reconcile
Home: green (yours) vs credit-room (gray) distinction not explained until the account page
Activity detail: '2 committed entries' wording is insider-language
No recurring-payout or weekly-summary view for gig income

personas.name: Priya
personas.verdict: The Receive screen with the payment link and QR is fast to pull up, and I can see at a glance which payments say 'settled' — but the closing-time reconcile needs me to open each receipt and Export CSV is buried in Activity.
blockers: No dedicated 'Request' flow — Receive is hidden behind a home button, and counter requests require the link/QR path
'Settled' verification is inside the receipt detail, not on the payment row
No per-day settlement total at a glance (must use Activity header or Export CSV)
Export CSV is a text link, not a prominent action

personas.name: Wei
personas.verdict: The account page tells me exactly what the hub owes me, what credit line I've given, and what collateral I've posted, and the book is precise — the only friction is that a cross-network swap forces me through a credit-limit step first.
blockers: Cross-network swap (05b): red 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' gate adds a credit-limit step before the trade
Collateral slider + 'Add 10% buffer' is more math than I want for a swap
Per-lane exposure is behind 'Ledger detail', not on the account card
Fee precision inconsistent ('under 0.01' vs exact 0.000050) on the Pay screen

personas.name: Elena
personas.verdict: Every receipt carries a frame number, a proof hash, and a runtime-verified stamp, and Sovereignty lets me save a full evidence bundle — but the proof hashes are truncated with no copy affordance on the receipt itself.
blockers: Receipt and activity detail: proof hash '0x00109fe5...6bec' truncated, no copy-on-tap
'2 committed entries' and 'committed frames' jargon
Evidence bundle is deep under Sovereignty, not beside Export CSV
Frame # vs runtime frame vs entity frame numbering needs a glossary to audit

personas.name: Noah
personas.verdict: The UI maps cleanly to the model (bilateral accounts, credit/collateral, frame-based receipts, disputes, atomic swaps) and the 'green is yours / violet is a promise' rule is a great mental model — but the legend contradicts itself and the identity is scattered across three screens.
blockers: Home 'two colours, one rule' vs account page five-state legend (secured/promised/you owe/credit room/in flight)
Runtime id, Entity id, Signer, Depository spread across Settings, Sovereignty and Ownership — need a single identity view
'frame #' vs 'committed entries' vs 'runtime committed frames' without a glossary
Swap 'atomic·both legs or neither' and 'bilateral·signed by both sides' are the clearest protocol statements but appear only in Swap, not in a model overview

personas.name: Aisha
personas.verdict: The cross-network swap shows the route (Testnet→H1→Tron), atomic settlement, fee and lot rounding, and a receive-into-Tron preview — exactly what I need — but the credit-limit gate plus dense copy is risky on a weak connection.
blockers: Cross-network swap: 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' forces a credit-limit extension (slider + buffer) before the trade
No explicit 'fee + when it lands' summary line — cross-network ETA is not stated
No offline/retry affordance seen for a weak connection
Dense tariff/collateral copy over a mobile connection is a lot to load and read

personas.name: Lucas
personas.verdict: Receiving $10 from a friend and paying are fast and the green/violet rule is simple — but every swap and cross-network move makes me read 'collateral tariff' and 'buffer' before I can finish a $20 trade.
blockers: Home 'Spendable now $175.00' over 'Total balance $155.00' is confusing
Swap: 'Limit price / Hub fee / Route / Settlement / Lot rounding' is a wall of fintech terms
Cross-network swap requires credit-limit extension with collateral tariff and buffer
Receive: 'Send the link... the payer just confirms' is good, but 'Note·optional / What is this for?' reads as unfinished

personas.name: Ingrid
personas.verdict: This product speaks my language — Manage splits total into 'yours whatever a hub does' vs 'promised by hubs', the account page exposes credit lines, collateral and uncovered exposure, and Sovereignty quantifies 'enforceable right now' per counterparty.
blockers: No single per-counterparty exposure total — 'Ledger detail' is a separate screen from the account card
'They owe you, uncovered $90.00' and 'Collateral you posted $60.00' must be mentally reconciled
'Cover it' purple link is ambiguous (post collateral vs extend credit)
Risk hierarchy (collateral vs credit line vs promise) is only fully clear after reading Manage, account, and Sovereignty

personas.name: Omar
personas.verdict: The wallet shows what a hub does — credit lines, collateral on request, disputes with a 1-day window — and Lending lets me see the hub pool and offer liquidity, though there is no view of what the hub actually earns from me.
blockers: No aggregate 'what H1 earned from you' view — fees and interest appear only on individual swaps/lending
H1 POOL shows Available/Borrowed/Active principal but no utilization or min-liquidity metric
Hub credit-line economics (their line to you vs yours to them) are visible but no consolidated liquidity/margin picture
'Hub fee 1 bps' and lending interest are the only earn signals, scattered
